Barns have since had a huge come-up and are now a hugely popular wedding venue. Regardless of your stance on barn weddings, you have to dress a little differently. Vineyard weddings (and really any outdoor event) live in that same category. If you’re looking at a late-fall event, you’ll want something a little warmer. The Grey Plaid Wool Suit is a step up in that department without being too overbearing; the subtle designs also scream fall. You can also go with the blazer-and-dress-pants route. If the wedding isn’t all that fancy, you can get away with rocking some of the most comfortable dress shoes/sneakers out there: Cole Haan’s Zerogrand Remastered Wing Tip Oxfords.

Reigning Champ Heavyweight Jersey OG T-Shirt

The destination wedding can definitely be a challenge, depending on how close you are to the person (or people) getting married. They’re always a great time, though, and you can get similarly creative. We suggest a travel blazer; you’re already shelling out a lot of money for flights and accommodations, so you can save a few bucks by not checking a full suit. #4995. Could Your GLP-1s Make You Blind? Here’s What to Make of the FDA’s Latest Notice.

For years, there have been rumblings and even research about a rare but serious condition that’s been linked to taking a GLP-1 medication. Now, the Food and Drug Administration is doing something about it.

The FDA just released a drug safety communication to warn patients and healthcare providers about the potential increased risk of developing non-arteritic anterior ischemic optic neuropathy (NAION) when you take a GLP-1 medication. NAION is a rare condition that can lead to vision loss in one eye, and it can be permanent.

Again, this isn't the first time concerns have been raised about the risk of NAION. But it is the first time the FDA has issued a warning about it.

Given that up to 11 percent of Americans currently take a GLP-1 for weight loss, this news stands to impact a lot of people. How concerned should you be if you're one of them? Eye experts and a doctor who prescribes GLP-1s break it down.

Meet the experts: Joseph Rizzo, MD, director of the Neuro-Ophthalmology Service at Mass Eye and Ear, a member of the Mass General Brigham healthcare system; Bavand Youssefzadeh, DO, an ophthalmologist with Cedars-Sinai in Los Angeles and a cofounder of the Global LASIK and Cataract Institute; and Mir Ali, MD, the medical director of MemorialCare Surgical Weight Loss Center at Orange Coast Medical Center in Fountain Valley, California.

The FDA's notice is designed to flag the potential risk of NAION to people who use GLP-1s. The FDA also notes that the agency will require all manufacturers of GLP-1 medications to add information about the risk of NAION to the Warnings and Precautions section of their labels.

"Patients and caregivers should be aware of a potential increased risk of NAION, a rare condition that can result in acute, painless, decreased vision in one eye, including permanent vision loss, with GLP-1 RA use," the notice reads.

The agency cited a 2024 study published in JAMA Ophthalmology as well as its own meta-analyses and retrospective cohort study in the notice. They also noted that “NAION cases have been reported for all currently marketed GLP-1 RA products.”

However, the complication remains rare: incidents from the FDA’s meta-analysis were just 6.4 events per 100,000 per year for patients using the medications.

The warning is just that—a warning to patients and physicians that this could happen, explains Joseph Rizzo, MD, director of the Neuro-Ophthalmology Service at Mass Eye and Ear, a member of the Mass General Brigham healthcare system. "Most outcome-related issues in medicine should be thought of as being probabilistic—there is a certain chance that events can occur," he says. "This warning indicates that the FDA has reason to believe, at least at this time, that the probability of NAION occurring is higher in patients who take GLP-1 RA drugs."

But Dr. Rizzo stresses that there's no evidence that these drugs cause NAION—just that there's a link.

So…why issue a warning if it's not proven that GLP-1s cause NAION and it's so rare? "The severity of a complication matters alongside its frequency," says Bavand Youssefzadeh, DO, an ophthalmologist with Cedars-Sinai in Los Angeles and a cofounder of the Global LASIK and Cataract Institute. "Even a rare risk deserves attention when it can permanently affect vision." The warning is likely designed to give healthcare providers a heads-up that it could be NAION if a patient has symptoms, he explains.

"It's their duty to report any adverse effects, just so people are aware of them," says Mir Ali, MD, the medical director of MemorialCare Surgical Weight Loss Center at Orange Coast Medical Center in Fountain Valley, California.

While NAION is scary, doctors say it's important to put the data in perspective. "It's extremely rare, but it can happen," Dr. Ali says. Given how much GLP-1s can help with blood sugar management, weight loss, and downstream health effects, Dr. Ali says that the risk of NAION is "not a reason not to seek these medications."

Dr. Rizzo agrees. "I essentially never discourage the general use of GLP-1 RA drugs," he says. "Ultimately, the risk-to-benefit assessment must be decided by the patient, but physicians should provide sufficient information to the patients to better inform their decisions."

People should stay aware of the risk without panicking, Dr. Youssefzadeh says. "It's also worth remembering that the people most likely to be prescribed these drugs—people with diabetes, high blood pressure, sleep apnea—already carry a higher baseline risk for NAION, so the risk isn't starting from zero," he adds.

#4994. Bitcoin Hits 12-Week Low as Fed Rate Fears Undo Most of Summer Rally

Bitcoin Hits 12-Week Low as Fed Rate Fears Undo Most of Summer Rally

Bitcoin fell to roughly $68,500 on Friday, hitting its lowest price in 12 weeks as renewed U.S. inflation worries and investor withdrawals pushed the cryptocurrency further into the red.

BTC was down about 4.5% over 24 hours and 9.5% for the week, according to Friday market data. Ethereum traded near $1,925, while Solana slipped below $80 as selling spread across major cryptocurrencies.

The latest slide has erased most of Bitcoin's late-summer recovery. But not all of it: BTC remains approximately 16% above its late-June low near $59,000, even after retreating roughly 21% from its autumn peak around $86,000.

Chicago Federal Reserve President Austan Goolsbee warned Friday that inflation had spread beyond energy and tariffs, with rising services and medical costs and demand from AI data centers adding to price pressures.

“Are we on a path back to 2%? My feeling right now is we are not and we've got to deal with that,” Goolsbee said according to Reuters.

Goolsbee did not explicitly endorse a December rate hike. But other Fed officials have been more direct.

On Tuesday, Fed Governor Christopher Waller said he supported raising interest rates by at least 25 basis points, or 0.25 percentage points, at the December 8-9 meeting.

He also established a threshold for considering something more aggressive.

“If the October CPI inflation data out later today are similar to the past two monthly readings—with core CPI inflation around 0.3 percent or even higher—then a stronger policy move may be needed,” Waller said in his official remarks.

The report subsequently showed core CPI rising exactly 0.3%, exceeding the 0.2% forecast and meeting Waller's condition for considering a 50-basis-point increase.

Markets have responded accordingly. Futures-based rate probabilities as of November 13 showed a 91.9% probability of a quarter-point increase and an 8.1% probability of a half-point increase.

Those figures reflect trader expectations, not a decision by the Fed. The central bank's current target range is 3.75% to 4.00%.

Friday's producer-price report added to the concerns. Wholesale prices rose 0.3% in October, less than forecast, but increased 6.5% year over year, the largest annual jump since 2022.

For Bitcoin, higher rates make traditional interest-bearing investments relatively more attractive, reducing the appeal of speculative assets.

Meanwhile, U.S. spot Bitcoin ETFs have registered six consecutive sessions of net outflows, totaling approximately $1.49 billion between November 5 and November 12.

Thursday's $47.7 million withdrawal extended the five-day outflow streak, bringing another source of pressure to an already struggling market.

That does not mean institutional investors have abandoned Bitcoin. The funds still hold approximately $55.5 billion in cumulative net inflows, but it does show the state of nervousness that investors are feeling.

Weakening ETF demand, combined with forced liquidations of leveraged traders, can accelerate a decline when buyers are scarce.

Bitcoin's daily chart now shows a clear sequence of lower highs and lower lows, confirming a bearish short-term trajectory.

Its relative strength index, or RSI, has dropped to 25.4. Readings below 30 are generally considered oversold, suggesting the selling may be stretched.The average directional index, or ADX, stands at 25.3, indicating an established trend. Combined with declining prices, that suggests bearish momentum remains meaningful.

There is still one longer-term positive signal: the 50-day exponential moving average remains above the 200-day EMA, preserving a bullish moving-average configuration. But Bitcoin's price has fallen below the shorter-term average, indicating that recent momentum has turned against buyers.

Immediate support sits around $67,650, Friday's intraday low. Losing that level could expose a deeper support area near $64,000.

On the upside, Bitcoin needs to recover $70,815 and $72,775 before challenging the stronger resistance zone between $74,355 and $75,937.

The combination of extreme oversold readings and strong downward momentum leaves room for a temporary bounce, but not enough evidence to declare a bottom.

For now, traders face two major macroeconomic checkpoints: the Fed's November 18 meeting minutes and the November 25 PCE inflation report, both of which could influence expectations ahead of December's interest-rate decision.

#4993. Gemini’s quarterly retail trading volume sinks to 3-year low

Gemini’s third-quarter trading rebound masked a deepening retail slump.

Crypto exchange Gemini has just reported its lowest quarterly retail trading volume in three years, despite an increase in overall crypto trading volume.

Total spot trading volume rose 18% from the second quarter to $4.5 billion, according to Gemini’s Q3 earnings report. Institutional volume climbed 26% to $3.9 billion, while retail volume fell 14% to $600 million, its lowest level since the third quarter of 2023.

Gemini said the quarterly increase in spot trading volume was “supported by increased institutional Zcash activity and expanded affiliated market-making,” but did not give a specific reason for the decline in retail trading.

Despite the retail slump, Gemini’s exchange revenue increased 7% from the previous quarter to $13.4 million as institutional revenue more than doubled. Retail traders remained its largest source of exchange revenue, contributing nearly three-quarters of the total.

A number of crypto exchanges also reported softer crypto trading activity in the most recent quarter.

Coinbase reported softer retail and institutional activity, with consumer spot trading volume falling 9% from the previous quarter to $23.4 billion. Coinbase chief financial officer Alesia Haas said “continued growth in prediction markets helped offset softer crypto trading activity.”

At Robinhood, crypto revenue fell 55% year-on-year to $120 million, offset by a sixfold increase in event-contract revenue to $173 million.

Related: Strategy stock sheds 5% amid MSCI index removal, Bitcoin sell-off

Gemini also got some help from its own prediction exchange, Gemini Predictions, with revenue from that business unit increasing 52% quarter-on-quarter to $796,000, though it wasn’t significant enough to offset declines elsewhere.

Gemini reported stronger prediction-market activity heading into the fourth quarter, with average daily traders in October running about 50% above the third-quarter average.

Nearly a third of new prediction traders were new to Gemini, more than double the proportion in Q3.

The company is also seeking to distribute its event contracts through other platforms. An August nonbinding agreement with Apex Fintech Solutions would make Gemini Titan the exclusive venue for crypto event contracts distributed through Apex’s futures brokerage to its brokerage customers, subject to definitive agreements.

Gemini is set to host a Q3 earnings call on Friday.

#4989. Trump’s First Democratic Picks for SEC and CFTC Could Reshape Crypto’s Regulators

Trump’s First Democratic Picks for SEC and CFTC Could Reshape Crypto’s Regulators

President Donald Trump has nominated four people to fill vacant seats at the two federal agencies writing the rules for crypto, in a bipartisan slate that could reshape the commissions that have increasingly taken the lead on digital-asset policy after Congress stalled.

The White House said Thursday it sent the nominations to the Senate: Nathan Anonick and Matthew Rowland for the Commodity Futures Trading Commission, and Kristin Johnson and Steven Levine for the Securities and Exchange Commission.

Each requires Senate confirmation. Notably, the slate pairs a Republican and a Democrat at each agency, with Anonick and Levine the Republicans and Rowland and Johnson the Democrats, marking the first time the administration has put forward Democratic nominees for either commission.

The appointments matter because of how depleted both agencies have become. The CFTC in particular has been running on a skeleton crew, operating with Michael Selig as its lone Senate-confirmed member after a wave of departures, even as it has pursued one of the most aggressive crypto agendas in its history.

Filling those seats would give the commissions the quorum and staying power to turn proposals into durable rules.

Both CFTC nominees come from the Senate Agriculture Committee, which shares jurisdiction over crypto market structure and will vet their nominations. Anonick, a Republican, is legislative counsel to committee Chairman John Boozman and was a lead negotiator on the panel’s portion of the Clarity Act, the crypto market-structure bill that collapsed in the Senate this fall.

Rowland, a Democrat, is a career CFTC attorney detailed to the committee who also worked on the Clarity Act and an earlier 2024 crypto bill. His enforcement-heavy background and party lean could introduce a dissenting voice to a commission that, under Selig, has leaned firmly pro-industry.

On the SEC side, which the Senate Banking Committee will review, the picks would replace two commissioners central to crypto policy in opposite ways. Levine, a Republican, is slated to fill the seat of Hester Peirce, the agency’s most prominent crypto advocate and the head of its Crypto Task Force.

Levine’s own views on digital assets are not well established publicly, making his future votes a key variable for whether the SEC’s crypto-friendly push holds.

Johnson, a Democrat and former CFTC commissioner, would take the seat of frequent crypto skeptic Caroline Crenshaw; at the CFTC she focused on digital-asset custody and DeFi and pressed for stronger customer protections and conflict-of-interest rules.

The timing underscores a shift following the collapse of the Clarity Act, the crypto industry’s marquee market structure bill that would have established more-favorable-than-not rules for most of crypto.

After the legislation failed to advance in the Senate, the SEC and CFTC moved to fill the vacuum with their own authority, leaving the industry to get its “clarity” from regulators rather than legislators. A fully staffed pair of commissions would cement that dynamic.

Those agency efforts have been sweeping: The CFTC has cleared perpetual futures on individual stocks, floated bringing crypto exchanges under federal oversight, and moved to define event contracts as “swaps.” The SEC, meanwhile, rolled out an “innovation exemption” for tokenized stocks, proposed rules letting investment advisers custody crypto, and issued guidance suggesting most crypto assets aren’t securities.

The nominations are the first Trump has sent for these seats in roughly a year, a gap that reflected turbulence around crypto appointments. The administration previously pulled its CFTC chair nominee, Brian Quintenz, amid a clash involving the Winklevoss twins.

The confirmation window is now tight: with the Senate heading toward Democratic control in January, Republicans have only a short lame-duck stretch to move the slate before the calculus changes.

As a clothing-obsessed style writer, few things frustrate me more than a white tee that’s see-through, shrinks after one wash, or hangs awkwardly. So over the past few months, I made it my mission to track down the best white t-shirts for women. A white tee that ticks all those boxes is really the ultimate wardrobe essential, says celebrity stylist Julie Matos. It's the layering MVP that looks just as good with jeans as it does under a blazer. The tricky part is finding one that nails the trifecta of fabric, fit, and finish. Too often, white t-shirts are overly sheer, stiff, or cut in a way that doesn’t flatter the body. But after testing dozens, I can confirm: The perfect white t-shirt exists, and it’s worth the hunt.

So, are you ready to finally discover the perfect white tee that you can easily wear all year round? Start with this tried-and-tested guide.

After testing what feels like every white t-shirt on the internet, the Agolde Adine Shrunken Tee easily won my heart. It layers well and looks great on its own—it’s a true staple in my wardrobe that I wear about once a week. It has a relaxed silhouette and shorter (but not quite cropped) length that makes it super easy to style on its own with jeans or under a blazer or leather jacket. Oh, and it isn’t see-through at all.

It’s made from 100 percent organic cotton and has that thick, substantial feel I love in a t-shirt. Its weight gives it a luxe feel, even though the design is simple. That’s why it's thick enough to be worn with a nude bra, but still breathable and soft against the skin. Plus, it holds its shape well after multiple washes—I’ve been wearing and washing this tee at least once a week for the past year—no shrinkage, loose threads, or pilling in sight.

This tee nails that lived-in, vintage look that makes it look like you’ve owned it for years in the best possible way. Matos loves this t-shirt for that “fitted but not too tight” silhouette, and I totally agree. It’s structured enough to avoid looking sloppy, yet still relaxed and casual. The shrunken cut adds the right amount of shape, flattering my frame without too much extra fabric. The length seals the deal: it hits right at the waistband of my mid-rise jeans, so it looks perfectly balanced.

Between the fit, the feel, and that easy, slightly worn-in finish, the Adine Shrunken Tee truly is the white t-shirt gold standard. I’ve been wearing it nonstop—with jeans and a blazer to the office, layered under a sweater, or under a zip-up hoodie and sweats for laid-back errands.

Read More: Agolde Adine Shrunken Tee Review

At $20 (and sometimes under given frequent sales), this tee delivers on fit, quality, and durability. Made from 100% cotton, it feels thick, structured, and substantial, setting it apart from other budget-friendly options (which are often too thin, flimsy, or sheer). The fabric is completely opaque (a must for white t-shirts), yet it’s still soft and breathable. As Matos says, “it’s a great everyday basic—clean, classic, and reliable.”

I find that most cheaper t-shirts I've tried show wear and tear around the collar after just a few washes, but not this one. The neckline lies flat without stretching and has remained pristine through multiple wears and washes. That’s because it’s made from heavyweight cotton for structure and durability.

The fit is relaxed but not oversized for a casual look. I love how put-together this t-shirt looks, even when I wear it with jeans and sneakers. I find myself constantly reaching for it, and since it’s available in so many other neutral tones (like dark brown, gray, black, and navy), I’m seriously considering stocking up on more.

The length, though, is worth noting—it runs a tiny bit long on my 5’ 5” frame, which can make it tricky to style with high-rise bottoms given the thick fabric. But if you prefer a little extra coverage, or have a long torso, the longer cut might actually be a plus.

This t-shirt from Old Navy is soft, flattering, and comes in a truly size-inclusive range (XS to 4XL), making it a reliable go-to for every body. The relaxed fit creates that easy, lived-in vibe that works with anything in my closet, while the standard hip length makes it long enough to tuck in or wear loose without feeling boxy. Made from 100% cotton, it’s breathable, lightweight, and has that slightly broken-in texture that feels amazing with every wear.

The fit and drape make this tee so universally flattering. It skims the body without clinging, and the fabric has enough weight to hang nicely without stretching out or looking frumpy. It looks great with jeans and sneakers, and is polished enough to wear under a blazer or structured cardigan.

Amanda Lucci, director of special projects at WH, owns this tee in four different colors, and she says she's going to buy even more. "I appreciate that it's thick, making it not see-through at all, and long enough to tuck into jeans without having to fiddle with it all day." Another pro, according to Lucci? It gets softer and even more relaxed with every wash. And how good is the under-$20 price?

The one con is that the fit runs slightly big, so I recommend sizing down if you’re between sizes or prefer a more snug fit.

Just the other day, my friend was wearing the most adorable boxy white tee tucked into her trousers, and it turns out it was from Cos. So, when style coach Liz Wendler told me this is also her all-time favorite tee, I knew it deserved a spot on this list. Wendler says its thicker texture has a nice structure and weight, so you won’t have to worry about it being see-through. It’s made from heavyweight organic cotton for a neat fit that looks very flattering on the body and pairs beautifully under a blazer and jeans.

Wendler says this is her go-to white shirt, and she wears it all the time in tons of different ways. "I am very particular about how a white t-shirt wears, especially after a few washes—this one is by far the best I have ever experienced," she says. And I totally get the hype. I love wearing this shirt to work because the thick, structured look feels very professional and almost tailored. It’s a go-to for pairing with wide-leg trousers, a thick belt, and a kitten heel. The only con? It’s not the softest t-shirt on this list because of the thicker, heavier fabric. While it’s definitely not scratchy, it could feel smoother against the skin.

I was impressed by the quality of this Pima Cotton Crew Neck from Vince the moment I slipped it on. Made from premium 100% Pima cotton, it’s buttery soft yet structured enough to hold its shape, so it never looks flimsy or sheer. The crew neckline is clean and classic-looking, sitting just right above the collarbone without stretching or sagging over time. And the length of this tee hits right at the hip for an easy drape.

Yes, it’s on the pricier side—but the luxe fabric, impeccable cut, and timeless style prove that it’s a worthy investment piece.

The boxy fit creates an easy, relaxed shape that feels on trend without looking sloppy, while the slightly cropped length pairs perfectly with high-rise jeans or trousers. It hits right above the waistband, so it drapes naturally without tucking.

The slub cotton fabric (which, compared to regular cotton, has a subtle texture with tiny variations in the yarn) gives it a lived-in, slightly heathered look, Matos says. It’s lightweight and breathable, yet still feels sturdy enough to hold its shape. Matos says this tee has a great relaxed vibe thanks to the boxy fit, cropped length, and subtle texture.

The fit and feel make it an easy go-to for lounging and layering. When Aritzia released its Golden activewear line, style contributor Lily Wohlner immediately stockpiled a few of the pieces, including this white t-shirt. I noticed that when I wear this tee without the right bra, some bumps and lumps on my back are more visible. This elbow-sleeve t-shirt from Banana Republic gives the simple white tee a polished upgrade. #4987. The 8 Best Workout Shorts for Women of 2026, Tested By Editors and Stylists

Our favorite pair is from, believe it or not, Amazon.

Women's Health may earn commission from the links on this page, but we only feature products we believe in. Why Trust Us?

I’ll be honest—working out in shorts was never really my thing. I’ve always been more of a leggings girl. I used to think flowy shorts felt too exposed and compression shorts weren’t flattering. But since I'm a style writer who lives a pretty active lifestyle, I figured it was time to give athletic shorts a real shot. Now, after testing over 20 pairs of workout shorts over the past almost two-and-a-half years, I can officially say I’m a convert.

Alongside stylists and other WH editors, I tested the internet's most popular workout shorts. Over the past two years, we evaluated them based on coverage, moisture-wicking abilities, comfort, size range, and fit. The result? A list of six fantastic pairs that we recommend for all types of workouts, including running, HIIT training, yoga, Pilates, and more.

I’ve tested a wide range of athletic shorts, but the Gym People High Waist Short topped my list for a few reasons: it’s super soft, has nice compression, comes in a ton of colors, and has many different pockets to store your belongings. Plus, said pockets don’t add any bulk to your legs—a rare find in a short.

My biggest pet peeve with athletic shorts is when they feel way too tight and restrictive. But this pair, made from a polyester-spandex blend, has four-way stretch that makes it feel breathable, light, and easy to move in. “The fit is a bit more compressive around the stomach, which gives a nice smoothing and lifting effect—something I actually appreciate since super stretchy biker shorts can sometimes feel a little shapeless around the hips,” says style contributor Lily Wohlner.While this short does offer some compression, it leans more on the stretchy side than super form-fitting, so it might not be the best pick for high-impact workouts. It feels supportive, but I wouldn’t wear it for running or burpees since it doesn’t hold me in quite enough. That said, the fabric is buttery soft—like, ridiculously comfortable—so it’s perfect for walking, yoga, and Pilates. I also love that it’s not see-through, so I felt totally fine stretching and bending without worrying. The only downside? The moisture-wicking could be better. Wohlner says she wore it to hot yoga once, and the sweat stains were definitely noticeable.Read More: Best Leggings For Working Out

So many WH editors love this short from lululemon, especially for running. "I hadn't bought a pair of running shorts in years, but given that I've taken up running as a hobby, I knew I needed some for moving in hot weather," says associate health & fitness editor Addison Aloian. This extremely lightweight short, made from polyester and elastane, stood out to her because it's light and airy and comes in a ton of colors. Plus, there's a little side pocket where you can store your keys while logging miles.

Fast forward to today—she has logged hundreds of miles in this short and says it’s her all-time favorite pair for hitting the pavement. But, she also loves its versatility because she can wear it paired with a big sweatshirt for running errands, to a yoga class, or during her weekly strength training sessions. It never chafes or rubs against her legs, even when things start to get sweaty. Plus, she says the four-inch inseam offers excellent coverage so her cheeks are fully covered while she’s out and about. “They never ride up or move around, which is hard to find in a running short,” she says.

Stylist Rose Lauture is also a mega fan of this short, but she actually prefers the shorter, 2.5-inch inseam option—it’s the shortest option on this list—for its super airy feel. Despite the shorter inseam, she never feels exposed, but opt for the longer pair if you want to feel more covered. However, both shorts have a built-in panty liner for added coverage, so you never have to worry about anything slipping out (IYKYK).Both testers commented on how quickly this short dries. After a run, Aloian says there were some sweaty spots, but they were completely dry by the time she was ready to shower.

When I reach for a flowy workout short, it’s usually this pair from Beyond Yoga. I’ve been wearing it a ton to heated Pilates classes (my latest hyperfixation), and the lightweight breathability is unmatched. It’s made from a lightweight, woven fabric comprised of polyester and elastane. Woven fabrics, as opposed to knit fabrics, tend to be super breathable—and the vented back panel and perforated material at the sides give this short an extra airy feel. I never overheat while wearing it, whether I’m sweating it out on the mat or running miles.

Speaking of, this short is the epitome of versatile—I love it for strength training when paired with the Spacedye Slim Tank (my #1 workout top!), but it’s also a great running short. Despite the non-stretch material, the waistband offers plenty of give (and is adjustable!) and the leg openings are wide enough to keep things comfortable without chafing or riding up at the inner thighs—IYKYK.

It’s also really flattering, especially for a short that lacks compression. The body-skimming, flowy silhouette somehow makes my lower belly look super snatched. I love wearing it for regular days running errands, paired with a matching tank or zip-up sweatshirt. My only small complaint is that I wish it were available in more core colors. Right now, you can get it year-round in two shades, but there are usually lots of fun seasonal options depending on when you’re browsing.

Have you seen a cuter pair of workout shorts? I love the retro design with colorblocking and contrasting trims along with the mesh panels at the sides and hem. It’s one of the few workout shorts I wear just as frequently outside of the gym as I do to break a sweat. Pair it with a simple white tank (or top in any other color featured in the short) and flip-flops, and you have the perfect vintage activewear fit. On colder outings, throw your favorite sporty hoodie on top for a good complement.

I’m also a big fan of the length: The approximately 5-inch inseam and roomy leg openings with notched hems at the sides give a leg-slimming effect and are also just super comfortable. It also makes sure I don’t accidentally show too much skin while running in my neighborhood or picking up weights at the gym. An added layer of protection there is the built-in brief, which, unlike many I’ve encountered, doesn’t feel like it's giving me a constant wedgie (I’ve literally cut them out of my shorts before, but I barely notice it in this short).

Another bonus? The mesh paneling I mentioned earlier is as stylish as it is breathable. Even when I throw it on for a run on a treadmill in a stuffy gym, things stay feeling light and airy.

I only wish this short came in more colors—I would genuinely purchase them all. Right now, you can snag it in two color combos, but I’d love to see a few more and maybe even a neutral option.

If you're looking for a buttery-soft workout fit, this biker short from Beyond Yoga is your best friend. The brand itself is a favorite among our fashion team, and that's because the fabrics, which are made from super soft polyester and elastane, are never tight and constricting, always smooth and soft (yet still contouring and flattering!).

Yes, the short is awesome for all sorts of workouts, but we also love it for running errands and, dare we say it, lounging, as it looks so cute with every outfit and feels so comfortable for all-day wear. Plus, it's moisture-wicking during sweaty workouts. Speaking of sunny days, the short also has built-in UV protection, because we're all about staying protected from the sun here.

The Spacedye Biker Short is also one of the longest options on this list, so it's a solid choice if you're looking for something with a bit more leg coverage.

I often wear this short to yoga, but it's compressive enough that it doesn't budge when I wear it for a run or to higher-intensity classes. According to stylist Kristen Saladino, the high-waisted fit makes you feel super tucked-in and secure without feeling constricted. And, if you need a larger size, this short goes all the way up to a 4XL.

I do wish there were more colors to choose from. As of now, the brand only offers two core colors in this short.

Sure, we love the lululemon short for running, but the Norvan Short from Arc'teryx is built for the trails—and that’s exactly what we use it for. Lauture gives this fitted short a big thumbs-up for feeling super light and breathable, especially on long runs. It’s made from 100% polyester, so it’s airy and helps keep you cool by letting moisture escape and regulating your body temp. And if things do get sweaty, the built-in moisture-wicking brief (with antimicrobial treatment) helps manage odor—so you don’t have to stress.

Got loose keys or headphones? There's a discreet zippered back pocket that fits the essentials, like gels, electrolyte packs—you name it. It also has a reflective logo to help with visibility if you're running after dark. Another plus: the split side hem gives you a full range of motion, which is great for picking up the pace.

Our only real gripe is that we wish the waistband were a bit thicker for more tummy support. It’s also low-rise, which might not be everyone’s thing—but Lauture said she was surprised by how comfortable it felt and that it stayed put during her runs.

In my experience, it's difficult to find flowy workout shorts that don't show too much skin, but this option from Alo shifts that paradigm. It's light and airy with its woven material, but it doesn't have any open seams, so you don't have to worry about the wind catching it in the wrong way (IYKYK). Plus, it has a built-in brief, which is awesome for added protection.

I also love the thick elastic waistband, which not only adds a fun design element, but hits at the perfect height on our stomach to offer a nice contouring effect. There's also an invisible side pocket to store all your small essentials while on the go.My favorite part about this short is that it's never clingy, so it doesn't ride up the thigh or need constant readjusting while you're working out. I’ve owned it for months and recently tested it during a 45-minute strength and HIIT workout as well as an hour-long cross-training workout, and I never felt over-exposed or uncomfortable in it. It's roomy, but also holds you in. Plus, the fabric dries super fast, so you're in good hands if you get super sweaty.It does run one size big, which you should note when adding to cart. However, if you like shorts that are roomier, I can confirm that this one still gets high marks even when it's a size too big. In my experience, it still felt full-coverage, airy, and lightweight.

Patagonia’s Baggies Short is a warm-weather favorite among our editors—especially the ones who love spending time outdoors, like myself. The short fared exceptionally well during hot hikes over the summer but does just as well in the offseason indoors or while active outside.

It’s easy to throw on, thanks to its comfy fit that completely avoids any unwanted cling (no camel toe here, thank you very much). Plus, it’s made from quick-drying, breathable nylon, so I never have to worry about feeling weighed down. I’m personally stoked to wear this short again while hiking in Cotopaxi National Park in Ecuador.

While it definitely has a sporty vibe, it’s versatile enough to wear around the city, too. In black, it feels laid-back and low-key—perfect for running errands without looking like you just left the gym. Toss on an oversized sweatshirt or a longline sports bra, and you’ve got an effortless, off-duty look. And if you get caught in the rain or decide to take a dip? No stress—it’s water-repellent, so it won’t stay soaked.

The 5-inch inseam is another win: not too long, not too short—just the right amount of leg without worrying about coverage. Prefer something shorter? The Baggie also comes in a 2.5-inch version, which is great if you want a more cropped fit.

Fabric is everything when it comes to workout shorts—look for lightweight, sweat-wicking materials that move with you, not against you. According to Saladino, it's best to steer clear of cotton when looking for athletic shorts, as it doesn't wick away moisture as well as materials like polyester and nylon. After all, you want to make sure you're staying totally dry in your workout shorts (because who wants sweat stains down there?).

Most shorts on this list are high-rise, which we found to have the most coverage and look the most flattering during our workouts, as they offer flattering tummy control. Many high-rise shorts also have a drawstring, which helps you customize the fit so it doesn't slip down or ride up while you're getting a sweat on. Some of the options we tried were low-rise, but we ended up ditching most of them because we didn't love the fit. However, the Arc'teryx pair on this list is low-rise, and we actually love that it sits nicely on our hips and looks flattering.

When it comes to the best length for workout shorts, you want to think about the inseam length, AKA the distance between the crotch area and the bottom of the short. There are some longer options for those who prefer more leg coverage (ideal for burpees and squats!), and super short options on this list if you like a lightweight mini short for running or walking. After testing, we prefer something right in the middle that makes us feel nimble but also provides coverage, like our favorite of the bunch, The Gym People High Waist Shorts.

After testing, we found that some shorts are better for specific activities. For example, the Beyond Yoga pair is great for yoga because it’s super stretchy and buttery soft, so it’s easy to move in, whether you’re in downward dog or trying to master crow pose. On the other hand, the Arc'teryx pair is low-rise, super light, and has a snug fit, making it ideal for running since it feels weightless and doesn't slow us down.

We first compiled this list in July 2024. #4986. Fed Chair Warsh Wants Answers on AI Inflation—and Bitcoin May Feel the Impact

Fed Chair Warsh Wants Answers on AI Inflation—and Bitcoin May Feel the Impact

Federal Reserve Chair Kevin Warsh will convene a public forum Monday to examine whether artificial intelligence will bring down inflation, drive prices higher, or replace American workers.

The November 16 conference in San Francisco will bring together technology executives, economists, and employers to examine how AI is reshaping the economy.

The findings could influence how the Fed approaches interest rates, a major factor in Bitcoin's price movements as investors weigh whether to put money into risky assets or safer alternatives.

Warsh has argued that AI could help companies produce more goods and services at lower costs, easing inflation without requiring the Fed to keep borrowing expensive.

But some of his colleagues see a different problem: The AI boom is already making things more expensive, while the promised productivity benefits remain largely theoretical.

Building data centers requires enormous quantities of electricity, computer chips, construction materials, and skilled workers. When technology companies compete for those limited resources, prices rise.

Fed Governor Lisa Cook warned in September that AI investment was adding inflationary pressure and delaying the central bank's return to its 2% inflation target.

If AI eventually allows businesses to produce more without raising costs, inflation could cool, giving policymakers room to lower interest rates.

Lower rates generally make risky assets like Bitcoin or tech stocks more attractive because government bonds and savings accounts offer smaller returns, encouraging investors to seek higher gains elsewhere.

But if AI spending keeps inflation elevated, the Fed could maintain high interest rates or raise them further. That would make borrowing more expensive, strengthen the appeal of interest-bearing assets, and potentially drain money from speculative investments, including cryptocurrencies.

Bitcoin is already feeling that pressure. The cryptocurrency dropped below $69,000 Friday as stronger-than-expected inflation figures fueled concerns about another Fed rate hike.

AI also has a more direct connection to the Bitcoin industry than most may think of.

Both AI data centers and Bitcoin mining operations need access to large amounts of electricity. As AI companies compete for power and infrastructure, miners face pressure to secure affordable energy or consider more profitable alternatives.

Some are already abandoning Bitcoin mining altogether. Hyperscale Data shut down mining operations at its Michigan facility in September to accommodate an AI customer under a deal potentially worth more than $1.2 billion. The same has happened with other big names like Coreweave and other former Ethereum miners from its proof-of-work era.

Meanwhile, AI's potential impact on employment adds another complication.

Fed Governor Michael Barr warned Thursday of possible “serious short-term disruptions” as businesses increasingly replace human tasks with AI systems.

Widespread job losses could weaken consumer spending, slow economic growth, and eventually increase pressure on the Fed to cut rates. But a deteriorating economy could also push investors away from Bitcoin as they look to reduce risk.

Warsh himself acknowledged in August that AI represents “a new variable” for monetary policy.

The question now is whether AI's economic benefits will arrive quickly enough to outweigh the costs of building it.

Monday's conference will not determine the Fed's next interest-rate decision, scheduled for December 9. But it could offer clues about how policymakers view a technology boom that is increasingly influencing both Wall Street and the crypto market.

#4985. Trump nominates Hester Peirce successor among SEC, CFTC picks

The White House also named a former CFTC commissioner and two CLARITY Act veterans as nominees to fill vacancies at the SEC and CFTC.

US President Donald Trump has nominated Steven Levine to replace former Securities and Exchange Commission Commissioner Hester Peirce, one of the agency’s most prominent crypto advocates, as part of four nominations to fill vacancies at the SEC and Commodity Futures Trading Commission.

The White House’s latest announcement on Thursday named two nominees each for the SEC and the Commodity Futures Trading Commission, agencies whose decisions help shape US cryptocurrency regulation, among other functions. All four nominations require Senate confirmation.

The nominations would replenish several commissioner roles. The SEC currently has only two of its five commissioner seats filled, while CFTC Chairman Michael Selig is the sole member of his agency’s five-seat commission.

The nominations come weeks before Democrats are set to take control of the Senate in January, giving a narrow window for Republicans to confirm Trump’s picks.

Related: House Finance panel chair says regulator actions on crypto ‘fall short’ of CLARITY bill

Levine, a Republican, was nominated for an SEC term ending June 5, 2030, replacing Peirce, who left the agency in October. Peirce was a leading advocate for clearer crypto rules at the SEC, helping shape its approach to digital assets as the former head of its Crypto Task Force, while Levine’s views on crypto regulation are less publicly established.

Trump also nominated Democrat Kristin Johnson, a former CFTC commissioner, for the SEC seat held by Caroline Crenshaw, whose term has also expired. Johnson’s proposed term ends June 5, 2029. Johnson has advocated for stronger customer protections and conflict-of-interest rules for crypto firms in her time at the CFTC.

For the CFTC, Trump nominated Republican Nathan Anonick and Democrat Matthew Rowland, both of whom worked on the Clarity Act. CFTC Chairman Mike Selig called them “two strong bipartisan picks” for CFTC commissioners and said he looked forward to working with them upon their confirmation.

The nominees would typically appear before the Senate Banking Committee for the SEC positions and the Senate Agriculture Committee for the CFTC roles. Following committee consideration, their nominations would go to the full Senate, where confirmation requires a majority vote.

This material, made from thermoplastic polyurethane, blends firm and flexible foam components to create a lightweight, responsive, and well-cushioned feel. The mix of stiffer and softer sections absorbs impact from every step and actually helps propel you forward. The Cloudrunner 3 is actually a touch heavier than its predecessor (by only 0.7 ounces), but we chalk it up to the upgraded plush heel collar and wider base that offer a bit more comfort and stability. I’ve noticed this shoe is super durable, holding up to months of wear and tear on city sidewalks. During my walks in this shoe, I appreciate that I don’t feel overly bouncy, but the cushioning is still noticeable and light enough to help me feel grounded.“At nine months pregnant, I need to prioritize stability and comfort over everything else in a sneaker right now, and the On Cloudrunner 3s delivered for me,” Andriakos says. “It feels firm and supportive (and not overly cushioned), which has noticeably reduced my pelvic and low back pain when I’m on my feet all day and walking a lot.” She’s also been wearing it for hybrid strength-and-cardio workouts, and while it’s not a super-flat traditional lifting shoe, the fairly neutral sole and structured shape and feel make it surprisingly versatile. “Plus, the toe box is on the wider side and roomy enough for my swollen feet, so my toes can actually breathe,” Andriakos adds.

After about four months of testing an alarming amount of shoes, the On Cloudtilt Remix is my everyday go-to. That’s because this sneaker takes everything we love about the original Cloudtilt and gives it a fashion-forward upgrade with a techy upper designed with “X-ray layers,” or semi-transparent mesh overlays that look super sleek.

This shoe is basically built for walking, too, thanks to the CloudTec Phase midsole, a walking-focused cushioning system designed so each “cloud” compresses in sequence, delivering a smooth, plush ride. The result is an exceptionally smooth heel-to-toe transition that feels natural and effortless during long days on your feet. It also has a moderate 7 mm heel-to-toe drop, meaning it distributes weight evenly throughout the lower body and helps keep the foot in a neutral walking position, making it a pretty universal pick.

Underfoot, the cushioning lands squarely in the Goldilocks zone. The Helion superfoam provides plenty of impact absorption, but the ride never feels overly soft or marshmallow-like. Instead, it delivers a lightly responsive, cushioned feel that keeps your feet comfortable during long walks, travel days, and hours of sightseeing without sacrificing ground feel or stability. Lightweight, stylish, and genuinely built for all-day movement, the Cloudtilt Remix is the On sneaker I reach for when I want my shoes to work as hard as the rest of my outfit. The sleek, streamlined look is super easy to style with everything from tennis skirts to joggers to track pants. If you ask me, it’s kinda the perfect shoe that combines everything on this list into one sleek kick.

My one note is that I worry about the layered mesh upper being difficult to clean if the shoe gets too dirty. Luckily, I’ve managed to keep it pretty clean, but I avoid wearing this shoe in wet weather or otherwise messy conditions.

Hate tying your shoes? The Cloudnova Form 2 might be your new favorite—thanks to its easy slip-on, slip-off design, which Andriakos swears by. That said, it still has laces if you want to tighten things up for a more secure fit. This is my everyday shoe when I’m heading out the door to run errands or pop out for a walk but don’t feel like wearing anything bulky or something that needs a full lace adjustment (just lazy girl things!). It looks super cute with sweatpants and leggings, and a boxy t-shirt on top.

Comfort-wise, the Cloudnova Form is a win right out of the box. During my testing, I found that there was no break-in period needed (big ups). The moderately-cushioned sole is super balanced, which makes it ideal for long walks and power strolls, and Andriakos especially likes that it doesn’t have the super-prominent “bubble” look that many On shoes are known for. Instead, it has a lower-cut silhouette that feels a bit more grounded and less bouncy.

Another plus: The Form 2 is made with a breathable mesh upper and a soft microfiber tongue, so your feet stay cool and comfortable even on warm or extra-active days. On the downside, it runs small, so it’s a good idea to size it up by half. Also worth noting: it has a high heel-to-toe drop (14 mm), which can put extra stress on the knees and hips. If you deal with pain in those areas, you might want to skip this one.

On only offers wide sizing for certain models, but this shoe has a spacious toe box for a roomy fit. Fitness contributor Nicolette Accardi has bunions and never experiences pain when wearing it. “Most sneakers that don’t come in wide sizing tend to irritate and rub against my bunions, which makes them throb, but not the Cloudmonster,” she says. “The toe box is surprisingly a perfect fit and lets me walk around for hours pain-free.”

This new version of the shoe delivers a cradling sensation while the foam slightly compresses to conform to your feet. The sensation is pillow-like under the foot while also offering a stable feel. Fitness contributor Talene Appleton notes that it's her all-time fave On walking shoe for its high-stack cushion, meaning it has a very thick foam between your foot and the ground. The 3 gets back to the Cloudmonster’s roots and becomes a good running shoe for intermediate to advanced runners again. That’s thanks to a speedboard that promotes a forward rolling motion, along with the aforementioned maxed cushioning. This has added only a little weight from the last model (6.6 ounces to 8.5), so you don’t have to worry about this shoe holding you back during long walks or runs.

"Whenever I want to feel super comfortable in my shoes but don't want that tight, locked-in feeling like I do when I'm running, the Cloudmonster is my go-to," Appleton says. She wore the shoe while moving into her fourth-floor Brooklyn walk-up, and notes it kept her feet comfortable all day. And while it’s great for getting your steps in, this shoe has that chunky look that’s super on trend right now. I love pairing it with tailored pants and a boxy t-shirt on top for that upgraded activewear vibe.

The heel-to-toe drop is also on the smaller side at six millimeters, which Accardi says distributes impact evenly on the knees, hips, and ankles. “As someone with knee issues, taking the load off my knees is essential, especially post-run,” she says. If you’re a heel striker and don’t struggle with pain in these areas, the Cloudrunner 2 could be a better fit.

If your workouts don’t fit neatly into one category, the On Cloud X 4 is the sneaker you’ll want on standby. Designed specifically for mixed training, it’s comfortable, responsive, and stable, making it equally suited for walking, HIIT training, and gym sessions. Unlike some of On’s chunkier models, the Cloud X 4 has a slightly lower-profile silhouette that looks and feels sleeker on foot, pairing easily with everyday outfits and activewear.

The shoe features On’s signature CloudTec cushioning, which delivers a comfortable, impact-absorbing ride without feeling overly squishy. Andriakos, who logs a high daily step count, says it’s become one of her favorite shoes for long walks because the cushioning feels nice and plush while maintaining a grounded feel. “The mesh upper is super breathable, so my feet don’t feel overheated and sweaty after long walks, and small design details (like the cool X lace pattern from above!) make it feel really polished,” she says.

The supportive lacing system creates a secure, locked-in feel that feels stable during lateral movements and dynamic workouts. “I’ve worn it to HIIT classes, and it feels super supportive, though I’d still opt for a flatter, more structured shoe for traditional lifting,” Andriakos says. The mesh upper is a nice touch, too, keeping things super breathable so your feet don’t get overheated or sweaty on long walks.

The On Cloud 6 Coast is a refreshed take on the brand’s classic On Cloud—but this ultra-lightweight version takes it even further. It keeps all the upgrades of the latest model, including the original slip-on, no-lace design and On’s signature CloudTec cushioning system. The big win here? It weighs in at just 6.5 ounces. That means your ultra-cushioned shoe is now perfect for traveling, long days on your feet, or hot, humid commutes. It’s built with an updated mesh that’s super breathable and ventilated—you can even wear this shoe barefoot!It also features a wider opening for a more inclusive, easy-on fit. I really appreciated this feature as a wide-footed girly. It also has a moderate heel-to-toe drop of 8 mm, making it a great universal walking shoe. Bottom line: this shoe is made to handle just about anything, which makes it a must-have in your rotation.

This shoe has a medium cushion level for that sweet spot that’s comfortable and light on your feet without being overly plush. The CloudTec midsole does a great job absorbing impact, making it a solid choice for everything from sightseeing and airport sprints to casual daily walks. The lightweight build almost disappears on your foot, which is exactly what you want when you’re packing light or spending hours exploring.

The tradeoff for all that packability and featherlight comfort is support. The flexible upper and minimalist construction can feel a bit flimsy compared to more structured walking shoes, especially if you need extra arch support or stability.

On sneakers are extremely comfortable, but Schaeffer says that's because most of its shoes have a bit of weight to them. If a shoe is too lightweight (under four ounces), it sacrifices function and stability, he says. But, don't get it twisted—these don't feel like bricks on your feet either. Most On shoes are between four and 10 ounces, which means they're the perfect medium weight that doesn’t slack on support.

A heel-to-toe drop, sometimes called a midsole drop, is the difference in height between the heel and forefoot (toe area). Schaeffer says to look for a walking shoe with a heel-to-toe drop that puts your foot in a neutral position, which will be different for everyone’s unique foot and step pattern.

Support and stability are the number one qualities you should look for in a walking shoe, says Geller. He notes that when arches are supported, you create an "excellent" platform to launch from, meaning the feet are in the ideal position for takeoff and landing. This can help avoid foot injuries down the line.

Geller also says that many good walking shoes, including motion control shoes, will have medial posting—a firm wedge in the arch that holds up the heel—and firm cushioning for more support. "Firmer cushioning will resist the inward roll of the foot [overpronation], controlling the knees and hips better," he says.

If stability is a priority for you, also consider shoes with a broader sole to minimize excess movement. The increased material along the sides and front of your foot creates a wider platform, which is naturally resistant to feet rolling or wobbling, says Geller. In other words, it's a great feature for walkers who overpronate.

"Whenever you’re looking for a good walking shoe, you want to find a great mix of comfort and stability," says Schaeffer. You want a shoe that’s comfortable on your feet, but the level of cushioning will vary depending on your specific foot needs.

Wearing running shoes for walking isn’t inherently bad, but it’s not always the best idea either. Shoes designed specifically for running tend to have significantly more cushioning to absorb the higher impact that comes with each stride. “This isn't necessary for walking and reduces your feel of the ground, which is problematic for those with any balance issues or previous falls," Milica McDowell, a doctor of physical therapy, previously told Women’s Health.

Running shoes often have a very tight fit for higher performance, a narrow toe box, or are highly supported in the arch, which are features a lifestyle walker does not need, says McDowell. That’s why, in most cases, walkers are recommended to opt for a shoe designed specifically for walking (or one labeled for walking and running).

#4983. Bitcoin slides below $70K amid thin liquidity, ETF outflows

Bitcoin fell below $70,000 as crypto sentiment hit its lowest level in more than four months, with analysts warning of institutional outflows, thinning liquidity and elevated leverage.

Bitcoin fell below $70,000 on Friday, extending its recent decline as investor sentiment deteriorated amid institutional outflows, tightening liquidity and broader macroeconomic pressures.

Bitcoin (BTC) is trading at $68,607.23 at the time of writing, down 9.2% in the last week, according to CoinGecko.

The decline coincided with a sharp decline in market sentiment. The Crypto Fear & Greed Index fell to 20 on Friday, its lowest reading in more than four months, putting it in “extreme fear.” The index last reached that level on July 8.

Bitcoin’s seven-day price chart. Source: CoinGecko

Vikram Subburaj, CEO of crypto exchange Giottus, attributed Bitcoin’s weakness to institutional outflows, tightening crypto liquidity and expectations of a December Federal Reserve interest rate hike. “Investors should avoid chasing short-term dips or using excessive leverage,” he said.

In a Friday report, 10x Research highlighted Bitcoin’s divergence from US equities. Between Nov. 5 and Nov. 12, Bitcoin declined 5.9% while the Nasdaq 100 gained 6.4%, suggesting the cryptocurrency was responding more to rising Treasury yields and a stronger US dollar than to technology stocks.

The research firm said Bitcoin was increasingly trading alongside gold, which fell 5.5% over the same period, as the US 10-year Treasury yield climbed above 5%.

Meanwhile, institutional trading platform Talos also warned that thin liquidity and elevated leverage could amplify market volatility. Its weekly report showed Bitcoin order-book depth across major exchanges fell to $72 million on Nov. 9, roughly 33% below normal levels.

“Liquidity remains thin while leverage stays elevated, leaving the market vulnerable to sharp moves in either direction,” said Tanay Ved, senior research associate at Talos. “A rebuild in order-book depth and a turn in capital flows would provide a firmer foundation for recovery.”

The selloff follows sustained withdrawals from US spot Bitcoin exchange-traded funds (ETFs). BlackRock’s iShares Bitcoin Trust (IBIT) recorded more than $2 billion in net outflows across nine consecutive trading sessions through Wednesday, while broader funds shed nearly $1.44 billion over five sessions.

Preliminary Farside Investors data showed another $47.7 million in net outflows on Thursday, although figures for BlackRock and Fidelity were still pending.

#4980. Microsoft 365 outage hits Outlook email and Teams calendars worldwide

Microsoft began a wider patch rollout Friday as the outage disrupted government email and Microsoft 365 connectors in ChatGPT and Claude.

A global Microsoft 365 outage continued into Friday, disrupting Outlook email and some Teams features.

Microsoft said in a 7:25 am UTC update that a patch had improved stability on some servers and that it was working to deploy the fix more widely. The update, republished by the University of Pennsylvania, gave no timetable for restoration.

The outage began Thursday, leaving some users unable to access their Exchange Online mailboxes. Microsoft said a process that handles secure connection became overloaded, causing affected servers to stop processing requests.

The company said it attempted to restore services by restarting infrastructure, redirecting network traffic and expanding server capacity. Microsoft said there was no indication of a security breach.

The outage also affected features in Microsoft Copilot and Defender for Office 365. In Teams, users had trouble scheduling meetings and sending invitations. Microsoft said most Teams calls and chats continued to work.

Businesses and government agencies worldwide use Microsoft 365 for email and scheduling. Microsoft reported more than 450 million paid commercial seats for the suite in an October filing. Exchange Online hosts the mailboxes and calendars those organizations use, and outside apps, including AI assistants, rely on the same service to retrieve that data when users connect their work accounts.

OpenAI reported errors in ChatGPT’s Microsoft 365 connector. Anthropic said the outage caused most email, calendar and search requests through Claude’s Microsoft 365 connector to fail.

The US Court of Appeals for the Tenth Circuit said its clerk’s office could neither send nor receive email for much of Thursday. Japan’s Finance Ministry said it was unable to receive email on Friday and Singapore’s Government Technology Agency told CNA that government email was among systems affected.

#4979. Dormant Bitcoin Wallets Wake Up After 16 Years, Moving $6.9 Million

Dormant Bitcoin Wallets Wake Up After 16 Years, Moving $6.9 Million

Two Bitcoin addresses that had been dormant since 2010 suddenly moved $6.9 million worth of BTC on Friday, bringing two early mining rewards back into circulation after more than 16 years.

Blockchain tracking service Whale Alert flagged the first transfer at 4:08 a.m. UTC on November 13, when 50 BTC worth approximately $3.44 million moved from an address that had not spent its original mining reward since September 2010.

Just over two minutes later, another 50 BTC moved from a separate wallet with an equally long history.

Both transfers involved Bitcoin originally generated through mining, rather than coins purchased on an exchange. Their combined value today was approximately $6,885,068.

The coins came from two blocks mined on September 8 and September 19, 2010, respectively. Back then, Bitcoin traded for roughly six cents, meaning each 50 BTC reward was worth about three bucks.

At Friday's transaction prices of around $68,800 per Bitcoin, their combined value had increased approximately 1,147,511 times, equivalent to a 114,751,033% increase.

That percentage measures the appreciation in Bitcoin's market price (what’s known as unrealized gains), not money the holder has actually made by selling (which would be known as realized gains). In fact, it’s unknown whether this was a peer-to-peer transaction, an OTC sell, or simply a wallet switch for security reasons.

The $3 valuation is also an estimate. Bitcoin barely had a functioning market in September 2010, with historical prices showing a trading range of around five to seven cents. The Mt. Gox exchange had only opened that July, with its first recorded trade taking place at $0.04951 per coin.

The transfers are part of a broader trend of ancient Bitcoin wallets waking up in 2026. According to Galaxy Research data highlighted in August, Bitcoin that had remained untouched for at least a decade was moving at a pace rarely seen in previous years. In one 10-day stretch alone, six wallets dating back to 2011, 2012, and 2014 transferred a combined 553.59 BTC, worth more than $40 million at the time.

Some of those movements have been linked to security concerns, wallet upgrades, or transfers to professional custodians rather than outright selling. Friday's activity adds another 100 BTC to the growing list of early Bitcoin holdings changing hands—or at least changing addresses—after more than a decade of silence.

The blockchain provides a detailed record of where the money moved, but it doesn't reveal who controls the receiving wallets.

The first transaction split the 50 BTC into two new addresses, sending nearly 49.99 BTC to one and approximately 0.01 BTC to another, minus a tiny network fee.

The second transaction followed a similar pattern, transferring nearly 49 BTC to one address and approximately 1 BTC to another.

Both transactions cost just 1,110 satoshis each in network fees, equivalent to approximately $0.75. A satoshi is Bitcoin's smallest unit, worth one hundred-millionth of a BTC.

As of an on-chain check at approximately 14:00 UTC Friday, the 100 BTC had not moved again from their new destinations following the consolidation, and no sale has been identified.

#4977. Functional Core Workouts Are the Key to Moving Better in and Out of the Gym

Add these 15 expert-approved exercises into your weekly routine.

I don’t know about you, but doing core exercises is my least favorite part of workouts. Unfortunately, though, neglecting functional core training can make a big difference in your total-body strength, and how you move day to day.

Functional training focuses on compound movements that engage multiple muscle groups simultaneously and mimic the way our bodies move during everyday activities. Functionally training the core, specifically, involves strengthening the abdominal muscles that attach to the pelvis or spine.

For instance, a farmer’s carry mirrors the movement of carrying grocery bags. “This is an example of ‘bracing and carrying,’ where you need to keep a tight, braced core to carry the heavy weight,” says Corrine Carnation, CPT, a personal and group trainer at Equinox and creator of the Better You, Better Living program. Plus, a weak core can lead to poor posture and an increased risk of injury.

But the benefits extend way beyond preparing your body for real-life activities and protecting against pain or injury—keep reading for all the reasons you should do functional core movements.

Meet the experts: Corrine Carnation, CPT, is a personal and group trainer at Equinox. Cori Ritchey, CSCS, is the fitness editor at Women's Health, as well as a certified strength and conditioning coach and group fitness instructor in New York City.

Time: 30 minutes | Equipment (optional): kettlebell, dumbbells, slam ball, resistance band, or Pilates ring | Good for: core, hips, back

Instructions: Choose 5 to 6 exercises from the list below. Complete 2 to 3 sets of the indicated number of reps for each move. Aim to integrate functional core exercises into your training routine once or twice a week.

As these exercises become easier with practice, challenge yourself by increasing resistance while slightly decreasing the number of reps. For example, if 3 sets of 10 reps using bodyweight alone feels easy, try adding a weight or resistance band for 2 or 3 sets of 8 reps. By the last rep of each set, you should feel ready to stop but not completely at failure. When in doubt, start with bodyweight only, then add resistance until you feel the exercise is challenging, but doable.

Pro tip: Exercises aren’t one-size-fits-all, so it’s important to recognize when an exercise is either too challenging, too easy, or not comfortable for you. Keep in mind that every exercise can be modified if needed!

Why it rocks: The suitcase carry prepares the core for real-life activities such as carrying heavy things by your sides. It strengthens the core by making you resist the urge to bend, improving stability and balance—the added grip demand is a fun challenge, too.

1. Holding a weight in one hand, stand up tall and pull your shoulders back and down to prevent them from rolling forward. Keep your core tight and spine neutral.

2. Walk forward for 30 to 60 seconds while maintaining a strong grip and upright posture.

4. Turn around and pick the weight up again, this time with your left hand. Complete 4 reps on each side.

Why it rocks: The halo exercise improves shoulder mobility and stability while strengthening your core. Moving the weight around your head causes a perturbation (or distracting force) to your body, forcing you to stabilize using your core. This particular halo variation has the added benefit of enhancing upper-body strength, targeting the shoulders, back, and arms.

1. Stand with feet shoulder-width apart, holding one dumbbell in front of your chest with both hands and elbows bent at 90 degrees.

2. Slowly circle the dumbbell around your head, moving it clockwise from ear to ear, elbows hugging in.

3. Return to start and repeat the movement counterclockwise. That's 1 rep.

Why it rocks: Have you ever worried about straining your back when picking something up or twisting? This move strengthens the core, improves stability, and builds rotational strength to protect your body during these movements.

1. Sit on the floor with your knees bent and upper body leaned back until abs are engaged (aim for a 45-degree angle relative to the floor). Hold a slam ball or dumbbell close to your chest with your elbows bent.

2. Keeping your arms slightly bent, twist your torso to the left and slam the ball on the floor next to your left hip.

3. Twist your torso through center to the right and slam the ball on the floor near your right hip. That's 1 rep.

4. Continue alternating for a total of 10 to 12 reps.

Why it rocks: The overhead slam exercise requires you to stabilize your body as you lift and forcefully throw the ball down to the floor. It also strengthens your shoulders, arms, and upper back while improving explosive power and coordination.

1. Stand with your feet shoulder-width apart, a soft bend in knees, and core engaged, while holding a slam ball at your chest with both hands.

2. Rise up tall on your toes and extend your arms overhead holding the slam ball.

3. Bend at your hips (hinging forward slightly) and slam the ball on the floor directly in front of you. Exhale as you throw the ball down toward the floor with force. Be careful not to arch your back.

4. Catch the ball on the bounce while lowering back into the squat position. That's 1 rep.

Why it rocks: The wood chop exercise helps strengthen your core by working your abs and obliques, which can boost your twisting power and stability, building strength and coordination.

1. Start in a half-kneeling position with your left leg forward and your right leg back, both bent at 90 degrees, holding a dumbbell in front of your chest.

2. With your arms straight, torso upright, and hips facing forward, swiftly lower the weight diagonally across your body to the right hip while twisting to the right. Then, raise the weight to upper left diagonal while twisting to the left. That's 1 rep.

3. Complete 10 reps, then repeat on the other side.

Why it rocks: Keeping your lower back and head flush with the floor while your limbs shift weight will engage your deep core stabilizers. Being able to lift your legs and arms from this position is essential for a healthy spine.

1. Lie faceup holding one dumbbell horizontally in front of your chest with both hands. Lift legs to a tabletop position with your knees over hips, your lower back glued to the floor, and your core engaged.

2. Keeping one leg at a 90-degree angle, lower the other to tap your heel to the floor. As your leg lowers, reach your arms above your head to lower the weight toward the floor behind your head.

3. Engage your core to lift both your arms and leg back to start, then repeat on the opposite side. That's 1 rep.

Why it rocks: This exercise recruits your abdominal muscles to maintain balance and stability. A resistance band offers an added challenge for the core and lower body.

1. Stand with your feet shoulder-width apart and your hands on your hips or relaxed at your sides. (Optional: Place a resistance band around the arches of both feet.)

2. Balancing on one leg, draw one knee up toward your chest, hold for 1 second, then return it to the floor.

3. Repeat on the opposite side, alternating for 30 seconds. That’s 1 rep.

Why it rocks: Planks help you build the strength to push yourself up from the floor, which is important for many day-to-day activities. Adding the knee drive challenges your upper body and core to stabilize, improving your balance and coordination with uneven movements.

1. Start in a high plank position with your right foot lifted slightly up off the floor.

2. Exhale and pull your right knee toward your chest while rounding the spine to bring your nose toward your knee.

3. With control, reverse movement to return to plank position with right foot lifted. That's 1 rep.

Why it rocks: This exercise challenges you to sit up and lie down without using your hands, which requires strong core muscles. You can do it with a Pilates ring, a ball, or no equipment at all.

1. Lie faceup with your legs slightly bent, heels on floor, and arms extended straight above your head. (Optional: Place a mini resistance band around your wrists for an added challenge.)

2. Engage your core and draw your belly button in as you slowly begin to curl your spine off the mat one vertebra at a time. Roll up to an upright seated position while keeping biceps by the ears and arms reaching to the ceiling.

3. Once you reach the upright position, gradually reverse the movement by slowly rolling back down to the lying position. That's 1 rep.

Why it rocks: This exercise targets the glutes and core, the muscles needed to lift your hips. It's great for anyone who sits a lot, as it both strengthens and mobilizes the hips.

1. Lie faceup with knees bent and feet planted shoulder-width apart on the floor. Place your arms on the floor by your sides or for an added challenge, extend arms above with your hands directly above your shoulders and your palms facing in.

2. Engage your core as you press up into a glute bridge with your knees, hips, and shoulders in alignment, and hold this position.

3. From here, raise your right leg to a 90-degree angle, keeping the stationary leg firmly on the floor and pelvis stable. Return right foot to meet left foot in starting position. That’s 1 rep.

4. Continue alternating legs with your butt lifted and complete 10 to 12 reps on each side.

Why it rocks: The classic side plank targets the obliques, which are essential for stability and rotation in daily activities. It also works your shoulders and hips, promoting good posture and alignment.

1. Lie on your right side with your legs bent, your right elbow directly under your shoulder, and your left hand palm down.

2. Lift your hips off the mat, extending your legs to form a straight line from your head to heels.

3. Hold the position for 30 seconds, then repeat on the opposite side. That’s 1 rep.

Why it rocks: It's similar to the suitcase carry, but levels up the move a bit by testing your stabilization, as you have to stay upright even though the weight is trying to pull you down. Plus, it boosts your grip strength.

1. Stand up straight with feet shoulder-width apart and dumbbell in left hand.

2. Extend your right arm out to the side at a 45-degree angle from your body.

3. Slowly lift your left leg up until knee is at hip height.

4. Then, with control, lower your leg down to the floor. Repeat with right leg. That's 1 rep.

5. Complete 10 to 12 reps, then switch the dumbbell to your right hand.

Why it rocks: It targets your obliques, but also challenges your other core muscles in a more uncommon position. Additionally, it works your spinal mobility.

1. Kneel on left knee with toes pointed to the right, and right foot planted firmly to the side of body, holding a kettlebell in right hand.

2. Rack the kettlebell at chest, then lift it overhead, keeping eyes on the weight.

3. Slowly lower body down until left hand reaches the floor, then continue lowering until elbow and forearm reach the floor.

4. Reverse the movement with control and return to start. That's 1 rep.

Why it rocks: It's important to train rotation because we're constantly rotating in real life. Plank hip dips strengthen the obliques and stabilize the spine.

1. Start in a forearm plank position with elbows under shoulders and knees, hips, and torso in a straight line.

2. Drop right hip toward the floor, then return to center.

3. Immediately drop the left hip toward the floor.

Why it rocks: This move is one of the best for training functional power, and it demands stabilization from your core.

1. Stand with feet slightly wider than hip-width apart. Hold a kettlebell in front of your body with both hands, arms straight.

2. With a slight bend in the knees and a flat back, hinge at the hips and swing the kettlebell back through the legs. Use that momentum to stand and swing the kettlebell out in front of your body, up to shoulder height.

3. Thrust the hips forward and engage the glutes and core as you stand up straight. When the kettlebell hits shoulder height, the knees should be straight and glutes contracted in a full hip extension.

4. Allow the kettlebell to swing back down through the legs, while hinging at the hips. That's 1 rep.

The best functional core workouts include bodyweight and resistance exercises that challenge the core in different positions and directions. Your core is not one-dimensional, so it’s important to strengthen your body through movements that involve twisting, bending, and stabilizing in all directions. For example, a traditional situp only engages the core in a single plane of motion, but a workout with a Russian twist (for rotational movement), lateral side bends (for side-to-side movement), and plank variations (for multidirectional stability) ensures you are hitting your core muscles from all angles.

Carnation notes the importance of first activating your core before jumping right into a workout. To do so, she recommends the following: “Act as if someone is about to throw a basketball at your stomach.” It might sound odd, but this cue can be really effective in helping you tighten and brace your core to get ready for impact. It’s best to practice this abdominal bracing technique before going into more advanced exercises in order to ensure your core is engaged and ready for action, Carnation says.

Rachel Tavel is a doctor of physical therapy, strength and conditioning specialist certified by the National Strength and Conditioning Association, and writer. She co-authored the book “Stretch Yourself Healthy Guide: Easy Routines to Relieve Pain, Boost Energy, and Feel Refreshed” (Prevention, 2020) and is a Forbes Health Advisory Board Member.
